The first 12 bits of the artifact key select a shard. Within that shard, four replicas are placed across two availability zones, with two replicas per zone. The client selects the least-loaded replica as the seed and sends it the artifact.

The seed verifies the key and streams copies to the other zone. It acknowledges the write once one replica in each zone has stored the complete artifact; the remaining two replicas are populated in the background.

If the seed fails before acknowledgement, the client retries another replica. Retries use the same key and are idempotent: a replica already holding that key returns success without replacing its bytes.
